title: introduce lazy schema probe with explainable hints and streaming rollback
author: Ava Chen
release_notes: Added a lightweight lazy schema probe that emits explainable hints without aborting streams; introduced a soft_strict mode for warnings-only schema enforcement; implemented stream rollback token and resume behavior for hard failures; extended OpenAI-compat layer to surface schema hints for function_call errors; telemetry to surface probe latency and failure clarity metrics.
description: Motivation: customers integrating structured output (json-schema) want early, actionable feedback when schema mismatches occur in streaming responses but do not want hard failures by default. This PR implements a lightweight "lazy schema probe" that runs a shallow validation on the first N tokens or first structural boundary, emits explainable hint events into the stream and logs, and only triggers a rollback+hard-failure path if the probe detects irrecoverable mismatches and service config requires strict enforcement. Changes: 1) runtime/pkg/schema_probe: new probe implementation that does minimal token/shape checks and returns a list of human-friendly hints (e.g., 'missing field "user_id"', 'expected array but got string at path /items') instead of raw validator dumps; 2) streaming runtime: attach probe to stream start and create check-pointing token (rollback_token) that allows rewinding to pre-probe state if a subsequent hard validation fails; 3) API: response_format negotiation now accepts 'json_schema:soft' and 'json_schema:strict' and emits hint events via the existing stream event channel so OpenAI-compatible clients get hints as structured events; 4) openai adapter: map legacy function_call and toolcall parse errors into schema-hint events when possible to improve backwards compatibility; 5) telemetry: new metrics probe_latency_ms, schema_hint_count, schema_failure_clarity (labels: missing_field,type_mismatch,coercion_needed) and tagging for probe sensitivity setting; 6) SDK updates (python): convenience helper to surface hint events and recommended prompt edits; 7) Docs and tests. Compatibility and safety: default behavior for hosted API is conservative: lazy probe is behind the feature flag redwood.feature.lazy_schema_probe and default off for older tenants; 'json_schema' without explicit modifier keeps existing behavior. Rollout plan: feature flag gated rollout to first 5% of traffic, perf monitor for probe_latency and request p50/p95; if 3 consecutive regressions in latency or error-rate occur, auto-disable for that tenant. Testing: unit tests cover probe heuristics for common schema shapes, integration tests simulate partial streams and ensure rollback token rewinds and produces consistent final payloads, fuzz tests for malformed model outputs included. Observability: console dashboard (telemetry/schema-probe) added to show hint distributions and top failing paths. Implementation notes: probe is intentionally approximate (heuristic-first) to avoid CPU blowup; it runs with a short soft timeout and uses cached compiled schema footprints to speed up repeated validations. Migration notes: customers who need strict enforcement should explicitly request 'json_schema:strict' or enable the Strict Schema Runtime policy. Related: builds on work in ENG-1121 (stream checkpoints) and complements the schema clarity metrics introduced in ENG-1203. Checklist: - [x] Implement probe + rollback token - [x] OpenAI adapter mapping - [x] SDK helper and docs - [x] Unit + integration tests - [x] Telemetry registration - [x] Feature flag and rollout config

review_comments: Diego Morales: How much CPU/latency does the probe add in p95 workloads? We should gate this aggressively and ensure cached compiled schema footprints are used.
Ava Chen: Diego, probe is bounded by a 30ms soft timeout by default and uses a per-tenant LRU cache for compiled schema snippets. See telemetry/probe_latency metrics added in this PR.
Priya Kapoor: Suggest clearer metric names and additional tag for 'probe_sensitivity' so we can correlate failures to sensitivity levels.
Ava Chen: Updated metric names to include probe_sensitivity label and added dashboard tile; also added tests for sensitivity=high/low paths.

Ethan Zhang: Edge case: if probe emits hints and the model self-corrects mid-stream, we must not surface a downstream hard failure or duplicate hints. Also ensure rollback token plays well with KV cache eviction.
Ava Chen: Added integration test 'test_probe_self_corrects' and fixed checkpoint_manager to mark token idempotent for resume in presence of KV cache eviction.

summary_of_changes: Adds shallow preflight schema probe with explainable hints, rollback token for stream repair on hard failures, OpenAI adapter mappings for schema-related function_call errors, telemetry and SDK helpers, plus tests and docs.
notes_for_ops: Feature flag: redwood.feature.lazy_schema_probe default=false; rollout plan attached to ENG-1287; watch metrics: probe_latency_ms (p50/p95), schema_failure_clarity, request_error_rate. Ops can disable per-tenant via admin API.
docs_updated: docs/api/structured_output.md and sdk/python/redwood/response_schema.py updated with consumption patterns for hint events and migration guidance for strict vs soft modes.
tested_on: local CI, staging cluster with simulated model partials, and a small percentage of real traffic behind feature flag
qa_notes: To reproduce: enable feature flag for tenant, send a prompt expecting strict json_schema output; observe hint events in stream header, simulate malformed model response to trigger rollback and confirm final payload matches schema or appropriate error is returned.
qa_checklist: Unit tests added for probe heuristics
Integration test for rollback and resume_behavior
Fuzz tests for malformed JSON fragments
security_considerations: Probe processes model output only; no new customer data export. Telemetry aggregates counts and path labels; no PII is logged by default. Feature flag prevents accidental wide rollout.
